passages.text: You don’t get your work done because you think: ‘It’s too cold! It’s too hot. It’s too late! It’s too early! I’m too hungry! I’m too full!’ By dwelling on so many excuses for not working, you don’t make any more money, and the money you already have runs out.
passages.note: Procrastination and the excuses that keep work undone

passages.text: Some are just drinking buddies, some call you their dear, dear friend; but a friend in times of need is a comrade indeed.
passages.note: Telling true friends from fair-weather ones

passages.text: ‘Too cold, too hot, too late,’ they say. When the young neglect their work like this, riches pass them by. But one who considers heat and cold as no more than blades of grass—he does his duties as a man, and happiness never fails.

You can recognize a fake friend who’s a flatterer on four grounds. They support you equally in doing bad and doing good. They praise you to your face, and put you down behind your back. You can recognize a fake friend who’s a flatterer on these four grounds.

You can recognize a good-hearted friend who’s the same in good times and bad on four grounds. They tell you secrets. They keep your secrets. They don’t abandon you in times of trouble. They’d even give their life for your welfare.

You can recognize a good-hearted friend who’s sympathetic on four grounds. They don’t delight in your misfortune. They delight in your good fortune. They keep others from criticizing you. They encourage praise of you.
passages.note: A friend who rejoices in your good fortune

passages.text: A friend who’s a helper, one the same in both pleasure and pain, a friend of good counsel, and one of sympathy; an astute person understands these four friends for what they are and carefully looks after them, like a mother the child at her breast.
passages.note: Cherishing and caring for good friends
